text: New decree changes rules for declaring product origin

HÀ NỘI - Products manufactured or assembled in Việt Nam are no longer automatically entitled to be labelled as Vietnamese-origin goods, as businesses must prove they meet specific origin criteria, according to a new Government decree to take effect on January 1, 2027.

Decree 384/2026/NĐ-CP on determining Vietnamese origin for goods manufactured and circulated domestically allows businesses to independently determine and declare the origin of their products without having to obtain certification from State authorities.
However, companies using imported materials and components must demonstrate that their products meet the prescribed origin requirements.
Finishing or assembling imported components in Việt Nam alone is insufficient to establish Vietnamese origin.

Trịnh Thị Thu Hiền, deputy director of the Ministry of Industry and Trade's Import-Export Department, said the Government has issued various regulations on rules of origin for export and import activities, but previously lacked a separate, unified legal framework for determining the origin of goods manufactured and sold domestically.

The new decree establishes a legal basis for businesses to determine and declare product origin, while providing a transparent and consistent set of criteria for companies to follow and regulators to supervise and inspect.
It also aims to prevent origin fraud and misrepresentation, curb counterfeit and substandard goods, and protect the reputation and brands of Vietnamese products, Hiền said.

Under the decree, businesses dealing with goods that are not wholly obtained in Việt Nam can choose one of two criteria to establish Vietnamese origin: a change in tariff classification in the four-digit heading of Harmonised System (HS) code, or a minimum Vietnamese Value Content of 30 per cent calculated on the Ex-Works price.
Businesses must also ensure that their production goes beyond simple processing or manufacturing operations that are explicitly excluded from establishing Vietnamese origin.
The decree lists activities such as repackaging, packaging, labelling and simple assembly of components into a finished product as insufficient to confer Vietnamese origin.
This means that operating a factory in Việt Nam, importing components, assembling them and selling the finished goods domestically does not automatically make those products Vietnamese-origin.
Companies must assess their actual production processes against the decree's criteria and ensure that manufacturing activities extend beyond the simple operations excluded under the regulations.
